Bulls: Ground-level photos where one or more bulls are the main subject, including stud and sale bulls
Cows: Ground-level photos where cows, heifers or calves are the main subject
Rams: Ground-level photos where one or more rams are the main subject, including stud and sale rams
Livestock: Ground-level photos where other farm animals are the main subject: ewes, lambs, steers, mixed mobs, pigs, poultry or horses
People: Ground-level photos where farmers, workers, staff or other people are the main subject, including portraits and people at work
Products: Product and packshot photos of bags, bottles, drums, feed, seed, fertiliser, tools or other branded goods, often in a studio or styled setting
Machinery: Ground-level photos where tractors, sprayers, trucks, excavators or other vehicles and heavy equipment are the main subject, when no harvest is under way
Harvest: Ground-level photos of harvest under way: headers cutting crop, chaser bins, grain being unloaded or trucked, hay baling, or freshly harvested grain and produce
Crops: Ground-level photos of crops that no Crop- folder covers, crops too young to identify, or bare and prepared soil, including close-ups
Crop-Wheat: Ground-level photos of wheat: dense stands of upright stems with compact, upright heads that are beardless or have short awns, green when growing and golden when ripe
Crop-Barley: Ground-level photos of barley: heads with long, bristly awns that nod or droop as they ripen, green to pale gold
Crop-Oats: Ground-level photos of oats: loose, open, drooping clusters of hanging grains rather than compact heads
Crop-Canola: Ground-level photos of canola: bright yellow flowering paddocks, or tall plants with thin green or brown seed pods
Crop-Pulses: Ground-level photos of pulse crops such as chickpeas, lentils, field peas, faba beans or lupins: low, bushy plants with pods, often with white, purple or blue flowers
Crop-Cotton: Ground-level photos of cotton: rows of bushy plants with cream or pink flowers, green bolls, or open white fluffy bolls
Crop-Sorghum: Ground-level photos of sorghum: tall, corn-like stalks topped with dense, upright clusters of round red, bronze or cream grain
Crop-Maize: Ground-level photos of maize (corn): very tall stalks with broad leaves, tassels on top and cobs on the side
Crop-Sugarcane: Ground-level photos of sugarcane: very tall, dense stands of thick, jointed canes with long grass-like leaves
Crop-Rice: Ground-level photos of rice: flooded or wet bays of grassy plants with drooping grain heads
Crop-Pasture: Ground-level photos where pasture or fodder is the main subject, with no animals as the main subject: grasses, clover, lucerne, silage crops or hay paddocks before cutting
Crop-Vineyards: Ground-level photos of grapevines: trellised vineyard rows, vines or grape bunches
Crop-Orchards: Ground-level photos of tree crops: rows of fruit or nut trees such as apples, citrus, stone fruit, almonds, macadamias or avocados, including fruit on the tree
Crop-Vegetables: Ground-level photos of vegetable and market-garden crops such as potatoes, onions, carrots, lettuce, brassicas or tomatoes, in rows, beds or greenhouses
Infrastructure: Ground-level photos of roads, bridges, rail, pipelines, dams, power lines, wind or solar farms, sheds, silos or construction sites
Landscapes: Ground-level photos of wide rural or regional scenery with no single main subject: paddocks, horizons, country roads, weather and sunsets
Drone-Fields: Aerial or drone photos of farmland, crops, paddocks, orchards, irrigation or other rural land
Drone-Livestock: Aerial or drone photos where herds, flocks or other farm animals are the main subject
Drone-Infrastructure: Aerial or drone photos of roads, bridges, rail, pipelines, dams, wind or solar farms, buildings or construction sites
Events: Photos from field days, trade shows, conferences, product launches, presentations and other organised events
Behind-the-Scenes: Photos of the production itself: camera crews, lighting, sets, drone pilots and gear
Graphics: Anything that is not a photo: screenshots, logos, artwork, maps, plans, documents or scanned pages
